extracted.intended_audience: PRSA members and public relations professionals
extracted.subtask_description: The PRSA Code of Ethics sets ethical standards and conduct provisions for members of the Public Relations Society of America, describing core professional values and specific behavioral guidelines (with examples) to guide PR practice and decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability and enforcement of the Code
rubrics_metrics.description: This Code applies to PRSA members. The Code is designed to be a useful guide for PRSA members as they carry out their ethical responsibilities and to anticipate and accommodate ethical challenges by precedent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on enforcement of the Code has been eliminated, but the PRSA Board of Directors retains the right to bar from membership or expel from the Society any individual who has been or is sanctioned by a government agency or convicted in a court of law of an action that fails to comply with the Code. Ethical practice is the most important obligation of a PRSA member. The Member Code of Ethics is viewed as a model for other professions, organizations, and professionals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advocacy (professional value)
rubrics_metrics.description: We serve the public interest by acting as responsible advocates for those we represent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members provide a voice in the marketplace of ideas, facts, and viewpoints to aid informed public debate; advocacy is balanced with serving the public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty (professional value)
rubrics_metrics.description: We adhere to the highest standards of accuracy and truth in advancing the interests of those we represent and in communicating with the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Honesty requires accuracy and truthfulness in all communications on behalf of clients and organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expertise (professional value)
rubrics_metrics.description: We acquire and responsibly use specialized knowledge and experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members advance the profession through continued professional development, research, and education, and build credibility and relationships among institutions and audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence (professional value)
rubrics_metrics.description: We provide objective counsel to those we represent. We are accountable for our actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independence emphasizes objective counsel and accountability to clients and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loyalty (professional value)
rubrics_metrics.description: We are faithful to those we represent, while honoring our obligation to serve the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Loyalty balances advocacy for clients with obligations to the broader public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness (professional value)
rubrics_metrics.description: We deal fairly with clients, employers, competitors, peers, vendors, the media, and the general public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect all opinions and support the right of free expression; fairness underpins equitable treatment across stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free Flow of Information (Provision of Conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Principle: Protecting and advancing the free flow of accurate and truthful information is essential to serving the public interest and contributing to informed decision making in a democratic society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent: Maintain integrity of relationships with media, government, and the public; aid informed decision-making. Guidelines: A member shall preserve the integrity of the process of communication; be honest and accurate in all communications; act promptly to correct erroneous communications for which the practitioner is responsible; preserve the free flow of unprejudiced information when giving or receiving gifts by ensuring that gifts are nominal, legal, and infrequent. Examples of Improper Conduct: giving an expensive product to a columnist to influence coverage; entertaining a government official beyond legal limits or violating reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition (Provision of Conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Principle: Promoting healthy and fair competition among professionals preserves an ethical climate while fostering a robust business environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent: Promote respect and fair competition among public relations professionals; serve the public interest by providing the widest choice of practitioner options. Guidelines: Follow ethical hiring practices designed to respect free and open competition without deliberately undermining a competitor; preserve intellectual property rights in the marketplace. Examples of Improper Conduct: sharing helpful information with a counseling firm competing for business; spreading malicious and unfounded rumors about a competitor to recruit people and business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of Information (Provision of Conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Principle: Open communication fosters informed decision making in a democratic society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent: Build trust with the public by revealing all information needed for responsible decision making. Guidelines: Be honest and accurate in all communications; act promptly to correct erroneous communications for which the member is responsible; investigate the truthfulness and accuracy of information released on behalf of those represented; reveal the sponsors for causes and interests represented; disclose financial interest (such as stock ownership) in a client’s organization; avoid deceptive practices. Examples of Improper Conduct: implementing 'front groups' for undisclosed interests; lying by omission about financial information; failing to correct inaccurate information; employing people to pose as volunteers in 'grass roots' campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguarding Confidences (Provision of Conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Principle: Client trust requires appropriate protection of confidential and private information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent: Protect the privacy rights of clients, organizations, and individuals by safeguarding confidential information. Guidelines: Safeguard the confidences and privacy rights of present, former, and prospective clients and employees; protect privileged, confidential, or insider information gained from a client or organization; immediately advise an appropriate authority if a member discovers that confidential information is being divulged by an employee of a client company or organization. Examples of Improper Conduct: changing jobs and using confidential information to the detriment of a former employer; intentionally leaking proprietary information to the detriment of another party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of Interest (Provision of Conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Principle: Avoiding real, potential or perceived conflicts of interest builds the trust of clients, employers, and the publics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent: Earn trust and mutual respect with clients or employers; build trust with the public by avoiding or ending situations that put personal or professional interests in conflict with society’s interests. Guidelines: Act in the best interests of the client or employer, even subordinating personal interests; avoid actions and circumstances that may appear to compromise good business judgment or create a conflict; disclose promptly any existing or potential conflict of interest to affected clients or organizations; encourage clients and customers to determine if a conflict exists after notifying all affected parties. Examples of Improper Conduct: failing to disclose a strong financial interest in a client’s competitor; representing a competitor or conflicting interest without informing a prospective client.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhancing the Profession (Provision of Conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Principle: Public relations professionals work constantly to strengthen the public’s trust in the profession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent: Build respect and credibility with the public for the profession; improve, adapt and expand professional practices. Guidelines: Acknowledge obligation to protect and enhance the profession; keep informed and educated about practices to ensure ethical conduct; actively pursue personal professional development; decline representation of clients or organizations that urge or require actions contrary to this Code; accurately define what public relations activities can accomplish; counsel subordinates in proper ethical decision making; require subordinates to adhere to the Code; report practices that fail to comply with the Code, whether committed by PRSA members or not, to the appropriate authority. Examples of Improper Conduct: publicly declaring a product safe without disclosing evidence to the contrary; assigning questionable client work to a non-member practitioner to avoid ethical obligation of PRSA membership.
